summary: Haywood County, NC: a 60-ft CCC-built Aermotor tower of 1933 inside Great Smoky Mountains NP; the NPS uses it today as a radio repeater.

facts.design: 60-ft steel Aermotor lookout tower with a 7 x 7 ft metal cab
facts.agency: Haywood County, North Carolina (listed as administrator); National Park Service uses the tower for radio

access.note: Inside Great Smoky Mountains National Park; the register calls the site a popular backcountry hikers camp. The tower is in use for radio.

visit.trail_note: The 1928 USGS description says the station is best reached by trail from the Ola post office.

events.note: USGS set the survey mark 15 ft southeast of a tree-braced signal and observing tower, with an observing platform in its top
Steel Aermotor tower, 60 ft, with a 7 x 7 ft metal cab, constructed by the CCC
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on March 19, 2007
Manned by lookouts who lived on the premises, on two-week tours each year from February 15 to May 15 and from October 15 to December 15
Watchman's cabin, per the register, once stood just north of the tower
The register says the National Park Service uses the tower today as a radio repeater

notes_for_editor: The NHLR page is undated, so the present-tense claims (standing, radio repeater, backcountry camp) rest on it alone. The register lists Haywood County as administrator while the NPS uses the tower; the arrangement is not resolved here. The seasonal watch has no start or end year in these sources. The 1928 USGS description mentions an earlier tree-braced signal and observing platform, not the 1933 tower. WebSearch budget was used up in this run, so no park history, newspaper or Haywood County source was checked; a search could add dates for the watch and the cabin. Access level public is inferred from the backcountry camp wording. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the advice to ask the park before visiting and not to climb the tower, and the note that the 1928 trail route may have changed, were removed because neither the NHLR page nor the NGS sheet says them.
